title: On Generation in Metric Spaces
claim: Whether generation succeeds depends sharply on two scale parameters, with distinct regimes separated by thresholds in a parameter plane.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, phase-diagram rectangles on axes, sub-captions beneath
description: Two side-by-side schematic phase diagrams, drawn in grayscale. The horizontal axis is labeled Adversary and the vertical axis is labeled Generator. Panel (a) has a large light-gray region labeled 'Not Gen. in Limit'. A small darker rectangle in the bottom-left corner is labeled 'Gen. in Limit'. Its edges are marked by thresholds ε on the horizontal axis and ε′ on the vertical axis. Panel (b) splits the area at height ε′. Everything above that height is 'Not Gen. in Limit'. Below it, three vertical bands get progressively darker from left to right: 'Gen. in Limit', 'Non-Uniform' and 'Uniform'. The bands are separated at ε1 and ε2 on the horizontal axis. Panel sub-captions refer to Examples 4.8 and 4.9. The eye goes first to the darkest band and the contrast between regions.
caption: Illustration of two generation regimes in a metric space. The horizontal axis represents the adversary parameter, and the vertical axis represents the generator parameter.
abstract: We study generation in separable metric instance spaces. We extend the language generation framework from Kleinberg and Mullainathan [2024] beyond countable domains by defining novelty through metric separation and allowing asymmetric novelty parameters for the adversary and the generator. We introduce the $(\varepsilon,\varepsilon')$-closure dimension, a scale-sensitive analogue of closure dimension, which yields characterizations of uniform and non-uniform generatability and a sufficient condition for generation in the limit. Along the way, we identify a sharp geometric contrast. Namely, in doubling spaces, including all finite-dimensional normed spaces, generatability is stable across novelty scales and invariant under equivalent metrics. In general metric spaces, however, generatability can be highly scale-sensitive and metric-dependent; even in the natural infinite-dimensional Hilbert space $\ell^2$, all notions of generation may fail abruptly as the novelty parameters vary.
